# React and Next.js integration

This is a source-preserving React adapter, not a rewrite of the motion controller in React state. Original HTML, CSS and JavaScript remain available.

Copy the complete generated package. The React dependency set is **Component.jsx, react-controller.mjs, react-font.mjs and instrument-sans-variable.woff2**, plus the accompanying license notices. Import Component.jsx in React. For Next.js, also keep NextClient.jsx and import it inside your own client wrapper. The supplied next-page.jsx uses the callback-owning react-example.jsx client boundary; keep that example file too when copying the example page.

The widget renders client-side after an import-safe, stable server placeholder; meaningful widget content is not server-rendered. No iframe is used. Source markup, CSS, SVG and motion controller are included in the generated controller module. react-font.mjs registers only the bundled font in the document because font-face inside Shadow DOM is not supported consistently. Registration is shared per font URL and removed when its last instance is destroyed. All other styles stay scoped to the component.

React styles are embedded in react-controller.mjs. Editing the companion vanilla buttons.css alone does not update the copied React widget; edit the source and regenerate its adapter through frameworks/generate.mjs in the repository. Outer host styles do not guarantee overrides for CSS variables assigned inside the source root.

Pass initialOptions for the original controller's non-function options and callbacks for its named function options (see the vanilla API). Updating initialOptions alone does not reset user input or motion. Pass the new options and change resetKey to intentionally remount with them. Callbacks, onReady, onError and remount options are published during the layout commit; a suspended or abandoned render cannot replace the committed widget's handlers or options. Existing callback functions can change without resetting input or focus; changing the set of callback names remounts. Do not pass ordinary callback functions from a Next Server Component: implement the callback-owning wrapper with 'use client'.

A ref exposes reset(), cancel(), state (when the source has state), and the original controller. The imperative subtree is isolated in an open ShadowRoot to preserve scoped styles and SVGs. External form serialization does not cross the shadow boundary; use the source callbacks/ref API, not an assumption of ordinary React controlled inputs. Supply your application's CSP allowance for the component's injected styles and local font.

A missing real-operation callback is never replaced by pretend success. The copied examples identify their local demonstration explicitly. Replace demonstration callbacks with real operations, handle cancellation/failure, and resolve only after the actual operation succeeds. A generated export is not verified until framework build, lifecycle and interaction tests pass.

The ten legacy Feedback examples explicitly bind their visible data-demo controls in react-example.jsx. This local binding reproduces the source preview's tone/show, add/clear, reset/offline, cancel, start/load and unknown-progress actions, including its simulated failure toggle and abortable timers. It delegates on the stable source root so reset can replace descendant controls, and removes listeners on instance replacement or unmount. The added Reset local example button resets only that local widget. Production Component.jsx and react-controller.mjs do not bind these demonstration controls. For application integration remove the data-demo controls and local example binding, or supply a separate explicit preview adapter; connect real onAction operations to the documented controller API. A demo completion says nothing about a server operation.

Cancellation invalidates pending local UI work. An AbortSignal is not a guarantee that a remote service rolled back a request; implement safe server-side semantics and refresh actual state when necessary. A local cancellation message describes this widget's state, not a verified server rollback.

The original fixed-size Bookmark and Follow controls need236px, Share240px, and Delete248px at their default unit size. They are not claimed to fit a226px container; allocate their source width or deliberately adapt the source sizing variables/styles. Other demos may retain their original scene layout. This adapter does not silently redesign approved controls or use hidden overflow to conceal them.

For source audits, serialize the component's open ShadowRoot subtrees, not just the outer React host: host.outerHTML omits shadow content. Strict Trusted Types or style CSP policies may need an explicit integration adaptation for the trusted template/style injection; a restrictive policy is not bypassed automatically.

Where the original controller exports mountPreview(), the optional preview prop explicitly selects that local demonstration. It defaults to false and is not a production action handler. Sources without a preview adapter reject preview mode rather than silently performing a real operation. The supplied examples for those sources use explicitly local callbacks, except the documented Share sample's user-activated Copy link clipboard action. Upload's companion local file input and standard feedback nodes are bound within the component automatically; no file contents are read or uploaded without your handler.
